newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens chief sticks by bullish earnings outlook.
newsitem.headline: Siemens chief sticks by bullish earnings outlook.

text.p: The chief executive of Germany's Siemens AG this weekend repeated a forecast for a 20 percent rise in 1995/1996 profits, but said the electronics giant's earnings were generally disappointing.

In an interview with Der Spiegel magazine released ahead of publication, Siemens chief Heinrich von Pierer said he saw no reason to deviate from earlier bullish predictions for profit growth in the year ended September 30.
"We confirmed again in July that Siemens can raise its net profit by about 20 percent. That remains the case," he said.
"Additionally there will be an extraordinary contribution in triple-digit millions from the sale of the high performance printer division."
Siemens posted group net profit of 2.084 billion marks for the 1994/1995 business year and its net profit at the nine-month stage rose 16 percent to 1.65 billion marks.
However Von Pierer also said that Siemens was earning too little compared with its international rivals. "We are at the low end of the mid-range, that is unsatisfactory," he said.
Von Pierer blamed the pressure on earnings on high wage costs, saying that Siemens had been faced with a seven percent rise in wage costs in the past year.
"That must not happen again under any circumstances, every percentage point costs Siemens 200 million marks."

Negotiations were still going on in relation to controversial plans which Siemens shares with other leading German employers to implement a law cutting sick pay to 80 percent of full pay, from the current 100 percent.
"We will have to wait and see what comes from that," Von Pierer said.
